subject: Residency proofing & standby-region wire-up questions
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Acme Financial Security <security@acmefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Residency proofing & standby-region wire-up questions

Hi Daniel / Acme security team,

Thanks again for the review call this morning. As promised, I'm sending the specific items you asked us to provide to validate residency and the EU->APAC standby wire-up behavior for the Private VPC deployment. Attached are: residency-evidence.csv (data placement hashes per tenant), network-diagram-v2.png (logical peering/egress paths), and the initial KMS sync checklist.

Two quick clarifications we need from your side before we schedule the wire-up test window:
- For the standby activation test, do you want a read-only DR failover (no writes to APAC) or full active standby (writes allowed in APAC)? We need to know because it changes the KV/sync gating and RPO assumptions.
- Are there any egress filtering rules (IP allowlist / TLS-intercept appliances) we should be aware of on your side that might block our control-plane callbacks during cutover?

Proposed times for the wire-up rehearsal (we can do a three-hour window): Apr 6 09:00-12:00 UTC or Apr 7 14:00-17:00 UTC. Please confirm availability.

I've cc'd Marissa (networking lead) and Rishi (security / cryptography) for follow-up items.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Attachments: residency-evidence.csv (CSV, 45KB); network-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 820KB); kms-sync-checklist.docx (DOCX, 68KB)

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@acmefin.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmefin.com
Date: 2027-04-01T13:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency proofing & standby-region wire-up questions

Naomi, thanks for the files and the options. A few answers up front: 
- For the rehearsal we want read-only DR only. Production writes to APAC are not allowed during this test window. This is to preserve transactional integrity for our audit trails.
- We do have an egress filtering appliance (TLS-inspect) in front of our peering edge; it can present a different TLS fingerprint and will break mTLS with client cert pinning unless the certs are admitted. We'll need coordination with your networking team to exchange the expected cert chain or use a passthrough for control-plane endpoints.

We'll take Apr 6 09:00-12:00 UTC for the rehearsal. Please share more details on the control-plane callbacks (destination hostnames/IPs and ports) and the exact certificate CNs used by Redwood's private-controlplane so our appliance team can pre-authorize them.

Thanks,
Daniel Cho
Senior InfoSec Engineer, Acme Financial

Date: 2027-04-01T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency proofing & standby-region wire-up questions

Daniel — great, read-only rehearsal confirmed for Apr 6.

Jordan and Marissa — looping you both in. Action items:
- Marissa: can you produce the control-plane endpoint list (FQDNs/IPs + TCP ports) and the cert CNs that Redwood will present? Acme needs these to program their TLS-inspect allowances. We should add both the hosted-controlplane and any private-controlplane endpoints used during the cutover.
- Jordan: can you confirm whether we can offer a temporary passthrough option for control-plane callbacks from the customer's peering to avoid TLS-inspect issues? If passthrough is not possible, we'll need to provide the cert chain and schedule a cert-exchange window with Acme.

Also: Rishi, their read-only constraint implies we must disable write tokens and any async fanout to APAC; can you outline the minimal steps to ensure no accidental writes during the rehearsal? A short checklist would be ideal.

We'll collate the answers and publish an updated runbook in the Drive link (see JIRA-1234).

Thanks all,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Residency proofing & standby-region wire-up questions

Hi team,

Short answers and what I'll attach:
1) Control-plane endpoints (internal list):
   - control.eu.redwood-inference.internal (443) -- primary control-plane (mutual TLS)
   - control-standby.apac.redwood-inference.internal (443) -- read-only standby signaling channel
   - metrics-collector.eu.redwood-inference.internal (9200) -- read-only metrics push
   I'll drop the full IP list in Drive (network-diagram-v2.png references these names).

2) Cert chain / CNs: we'll present CN=control.redwood-inference.com for the primary and CN=control-standby.redwood-inference.com for the standby. Full cert chain (leaf + intermediate) will be uploaded to the drive share and we can do a cert-exchange during the Apr 4 maintenance window if that works for Acme.

3) Passthrough option: the customer's peering has the ability to create a passthrough ACL for the control-plane IPs. That's a configuration on the peering appliance. If Acme prefers we can coordinate a short maintenance window to open passthrough for the three-hour rehearsal.

Attachments in this message: kms-sync-checklist.docx (we updated step 4 to indicate explicit write-token disablement).

I'll be available on Apr 6 in the rehearsal channel (Slack link in the Drive doc).

- Jordan
Network Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency proofing & standby-region wire-up questions -- final checklist

Thanks everyone — concise final checklist below for the Apr 6 09:00-12:00 UTC rehearsal (read-only):
- Redwood will disable write tokens for tenants under the rehearsal scope (see kms-sync-checklist.docx step 4).
- Control-plane endpoints to be pre-authorized by Acme: control.redwood-inference.com (443), control-standby.redwood-inference.com (443), metrics-collector.eu.redwood-inference.com (9200).
- Acme to configure passthrough or allow the presented cert CNs (control.redwood-inference.com, control-standby.redwood-inference.com) in TLS-inspect.
- Marissa/Jordan to monitor network-level reachability during the first 15 minutes and escalate if mTLS handshake fails.
- Naomi to publish the rehearsal runbook and the Google Drive package to the link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-residency-evidence and attach JIRA-1234 for post-rehearsal notes.

If there are no objections, we'll treat this as the final operational checklist and proceed.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Cryptography | Redwood Inference
